verdict.rationale: Temporal documents SDKs with APIs for Workflow and Activity execution, a Temporal Client that bridges applications to the Temporal Service, and an official CLI. It is explicitly Workflows-as-Code, so developers can write their own code to integrate with external systems. However, the evidence never documents a dedicated connector or private-integration framework; custom integrations are only implied through Activities and the orchestration of 'any models, tools, systems'. missing for 10: explicit documentation of building custom connectors or private integrations, independent hands-on corroboration of integration-building via the SDKs.

support.subject: As a developer, I can build a custom connector or private integration with a documented developer platform, SDK, or CLI

citations.quote: They feature APIs for Workflow and Activity execution, automatic retries, and resilience mechanisms, making it easier to build fault-tolerant applications.
A Temporal Client acts as the bridge for communication between your applications and the Temporal Service, enabling you to start Workflow Executions, send Signals and Queries, and retrieve results.
Temporal isn't a no-code Workflow engine — it is Workflows-as-Code.
Use it to manage, monitor, and debug Temporal applications, plus run an embedded development service when you need fast local feedback.
Orchestrate your workflows, AI apps, and agents across any models, tools, systems, and length of time.
